translations.text: The Liturgy of Saint James the Apostle, brother of the Lord, first archbishop of Jerusalem. When the priest is preparing to celebrate the liturgy, he first says this prayer:
O God, as we enter this holy temple of your glory, make us your servants worthy to glorify your holy name.
For you are a merciful God who loves mankind, and to you we offer up glory, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
Prayer for laying out the holy prosphora: O Lord our God, who gave the bread of heaven as food for all the faithful, our Lord Jesus Christ, your only-begotten Son,
whom you sent down from heaven for our life, through whom you willed our salvation and care [?], through whom you blessed and sanctified us: bless this offering that has been set out, and receive it
on your heavenly altar as a sacrifice, as a sweet-smelling fragrance pleasing to you, as a mystery. And since you are merciful and love mankind, remember all who have brought this offering.
And grant us our request, and let it not be for our condemnation, nor for judgment and reproof, but for eternal salvation.
Second prayer for the laying out: O Lord our God, who called us to the true light that enlightens every person coming into the world,
be merciful to our sins and forgive our transgressions, and make us worthy of your holy mysteries. For you reign, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Third prayer. O Lord God, giver of life and distributor of every good thing, who gave mankind the hope of eternal life, our Lord and God Jesus Christ:
make us worthy in your holiness to perform this divine service to you with these good things that have been prepared, so that we may be kept by the power
of you, and at all times may offer up glory to you, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
When the priest puts on his vestments for the liturgy, he says this prayer:
You who clothed yourself with light as with a garment, appeared on earth in inexpressible humility, lived among people, and became our high priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek;
you who adorned your Church with truth, O Lord Almighty, and granted us the garment of heaven and incorruption: by your grace, make me worthy, as I now approach this divine heavenly service,
to strip off all defilement like a soiled garment. Adorn my soul with radiance and my body with holiness.
Remove my sins from me and scatter my iniquities away from me, and clothe me with virtue, holiness and steadfastness, so that, clothed by you
with the grace of the priesthood, I may become worthy to enter your holy place with those who kept your holy commandments without going astray, and that I may be found at the heavenly
wedding with the wise holy virgins, to sing your glory, Christ our God, who took away all sins. For you are
the sanctifier of our souls and bodies, and to you we offer up glory, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
When he goes up to the altar, he shall say these three prayers. He shall make the sign of the cross over the incense, and as he says each prayer he shall put on incense.
First prayer: Good King, Creator of all created things:
accept what they offer through your Church by the hands of your Christ. Bring about what is good for each person, lead all to perfection, and make us worthy of your grace and holiness.
For you are a merciful God who loves humankind, and we offer glory to you, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
Second prayer: Lord our God, who accepted the offering of Abel and Noah and Abraham, the sacrifice of Aaron and Samuel, and the incense of Zechariah:
accept this incense as a sweet fragrance from the hands of us sinners.
Forgive our sins, for blessed, holy and glorious is the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
Third prayer: God Almighty, Lord of great name, you have granted us entry into the Holy of Holies through the coming of your only-begotten Son. We ask and
beseech you, for we are afraid and trembling as we prepare to stand before your fearful, awesome and glorious altar.
Send your good grace down upon us. Give life to our souls and bodies, and make our minds firm in the true faith,
so that with a pure heart we may offer this offering, given from the fruits of the earth, for the forgiveness of sins and for the atonement of all your people.
Through the grace and love for humankind of your Christ: with him, and with the Holy Spirit, glory is your due, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
The deacon shall say the litany. The priest shall put on incense. They shall take up the [?], and they shall go up to the altar.
Prayer before the "Holy God": You are holy, our God, who dwell among the holy ones and sit on thrones of glory. You are holy,
you, our God, who are worshipped and glorified by the holy angels and archangels and by all the powers of heaven. You are holy, you, our God, who
receive the thrice-holy hymn from the six-winged seraphim: receive the thrice-holy hymn from us also, your unworthy servants, and have mercy on us. Spoken aloud:

For you are holy, our God, and you rest among the holy ones, and we offer the thrice-holy hymn to you, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. The people: Amen. And they shall say the "Holy God."
Prayer after the "Holy God."
Merciful, compassionate, patient, abundant in mercy and true Lord: look down from your prepared dwelling place and deliver us from every temptation of the devil and of humans, and
do not take your help away from us. We cannot overcome those who come against us, but you are able to rescue us from all who attack us.
Save us, Lord our God, from all the enemies of this world, so that we may enter your holy temple with pure thoughts and [carry out] your pleasing divine service

let us accomplish, so that we may be made worthy of eternal life. For yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Priest: + Peace to all. People: And with your spirit. Deacon: The fifth psalm of David. They say the psalm, and the readings are read.
Prayer before the Gospel. We thank you, Lord, who made light shine out of darkness and opened the eyes of our minds to look upon your commandments, and opened our mouths
to confess our sins and to practise your commandments. Lord, accept the prayer of your sinful and unworthy servants, and do not disregard our supplication, but according to your
great goodness, protect those who have come and those who are going to come to pray with us, and make the light of your divine words shine in our hearts and in theirs.

Exclamation: For you are the bringer of good news and the one who gives light, the resurrection and life of our souls and bodies, O our God, and to you we offer up glory, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen. Deacon: Stand upright and hear the holy Gospel. Priest: + Peace to all.
People: And with your spirit. And the reader shall announce the reading of the holy Gospel by its chapter heading. People: Glory to you, O Lord.
Deacon: Be attentive. After the reading of the Gospel, the deacon shall say the catholic litany of 12 petitions, together with "Christianity" [?].
The priest shall say this prayer: O God, who have let us hear the divine words, make our souls wise and enlighten them with the spiritual wisdom that has just been read, for salvation,
so that we may not only be hearers of these life-giving praises, but may also be doers of good works, striving in faith, with blameless conduct and a spotless life.
Exclamation: Through Christ Jesus our Lord, with whom glory befits you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. People:
And with your spirit. Deacon: Let us bow our heads to the Lord. People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: Send down your grace, O Lord our God, upon these who have bowed their heads and await your blessing.
Shepherd your people and bless your inheritance, and grant to all of us that we may all set our minds on what is yours, speak every day of what is yours, and walk in your commandments.
Exclamation: May your name be blessed and glorified, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen. Deacon: Let us sing in peace. And they shall say the hymn of the washing of hands.
Deacon: Let no one who is weak, let no one who is unworthy, let no one who is unable [remain], but recognize one another. Stand up, all of you.
And they shall say the hymn of holiness. Deacon: In wisdom, be attentive. People: Shall say the Creed. Deacon:
Let us stand well; let us all be attentive together; let us pray to the Lord. People: Kyrie eleison. Before the kiss, the priest shall say this prayer:
Prayer of holy James the apostle, first bishop of Jerusalem.
You who are God and Lord of all, O lover of mankind, who have made us, unworthy as we are, worthy of this hour, so that, cleansed of all deceit and all hypocrisy, we may be united
…united with one another by the holy kiss, established in the firmness of love and peace, [serving] your Godhead in holiness, through our Lord and God Jesus Christ.
Exclamation: For you are the God of peace, love and love for humankind, and to you we offer glory, to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever.
The people: Amen. The priest: Peace be with all. The people: And with your spirit. The deacon: Let us greet one another with a kiss in holy love.
After the kiss, the deacon says: Let us bow our heads to the Lord. The people: To you, O Lord.
The priest says this prayer: You who alone are Lord and merciful God, [look upon] those who now bow their necks before your holy altar and ask for
the spiritual gift that comes from you. Send down your blessing and bless them all with a spiritual blessing, you who dwell on high and look upon the lowly.
Exclamation: For your name is praised and worshipped, of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever.
The people: Amen. The deacon bows to the priest and says: Kyrie eleison.
The priest makes the sign of the cross and says to him: May the Lord accept your service. The deacon says the catholic litany, adding only this to it:

And for this holy, spotless sacrifice of offering that has been prepared beforehand and set out, and for those who bring it, and for this honorable priest who stands here and worthily offers it, let us all pray to the Lord God.
The people say Kyrie eleison three times. While the deacon is saying this, the priest offers this prayer for himself, saying the following three times:
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among people. And this three times.
O Lord, I will open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise. And this three times.
Fill my mouth with praise, so that we may sing of your glory, and of your great beauty all day long. And this three times.
Of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen. And he adds only this prayer:
O Lord, you have looked upon us with mercy and compassion, and have granted to us, your poor and unworthy servants, the boldness to stand before your holy
altar and to offer to you this reasonable, bloodless sacrifice for our sins. Look upon me, your useless servant, and blot out my
transgressions by your mercy. Purify my lips and my heart from every defilement of flesh and spirit. Remove from me every unseemly and
foolish thought, and make me able, by the power of the Holy Spirit, to offer this sacrifice. Have mercy on me for the sake of your goodness, as I draw near to your holy
altar. And may it please you, O Lord, that the offering which I offer with my hands be acceptable, with forgiveness according to my weakness. Do not cast me away
from your face, O Lord, and do not count this unworthiness of mine as defilement. Instead, have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy, and according to the multitude of your compassions
take away [?] my iniquities from me, so that, having come before your glory without condemnation, I may be made worthy of the shelter of your only-begotten Son, and
so that I may not promise freedom to others and grant this through your boundless love for mankind, while I myself am found useless as a slave of sin. O Master, almighty Lord, hear the supplication
of mine, for you are the one who gives help to all, and we all ask for the mercy that comes from you, from the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
The priest shall say: I beseech you, fathers and brothers, pray for me. And those standing with him shall answer: The Lord be with you. And he shall say this prayer:
O God, who by your inexpressible and boundless love for mankind sent your only-begotten Son into the world to bring back anew the stray
sheep, do not turn away from us who have taken in hand this awesome and bloodless offering of sacrifice, for we do not trust in our own righteous deeds
but in your mercies, by which you care for our race. We beseech and pray to your [?] (the text reads "of the gospel") that it may not be for the condemnation of your people,
this prepared mystery which you have given us for salvation, but rather for the blotting out of sins and the renewal of souls and bodies, and for being well-pleasing to you.
Exclamation: By the grace and mercy and love for mankind of your only-begotten Son, with whom you are blessed, together with your all-holy,
good and life-giving Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. People: Amen.
Priest: Peace to all. People: And with your spirit. Deacon:
Let us stand well, let us stand attentively, let us stand in fear. Attend to this holy offering, for we offer a sacrifice to God.
People: Mercy, peace, an offering of praise. The deacon shall lift the veil according to the rule.
The priest shall say the prayer: O Lord, King of the ages, great and glorious God, incline your ear and hear me, this sinner, and accept this holy offering set before you,
as you accepted the sacrifice of Abel, the offering of Noah, the whole burnt offering of Abraham, the priestly services of Moses and Aaron, the peace offering of Samuel, and David's
complete repentance; and as you accepted true service from the hands of your holy apostles, so now too, for you are the same God, have mercy on us for the sake of your holy name.
Exclamation: The love + of God the Father, + the grace + of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, and the communion of the all-holy Spirit be with you all.
People: And with your spirit. Priest: Let your hearts be on high. People: We have them with the Lord.
Priest: Let us give thanks to the Lord. People: It is fitting and right.
The priest shall say this prayer: Since + it is truly fitting and right and seemly, and we are bound to praise you, to sing hymns to you, to bless you,
to glorify you, to worship you, to give thanks to you, who are the Creator of all creatures, visible and invisible, the treasure of eternal good things,
who are the fountain of life for all, God and Lord, to whom the heavens sing praise, and the heavens of heavens and all their powers, the sun and the moon and all the ordered ranks
of the stars, the earth, the sea and all that is in it, the heavenly Jerusalem, the assembly, the church of the firstborn who are written in heaven, the spirits of the righteous and
prophets, the spirits of the apostles and of the martyrs, angels, archangels, thrones, dominions, principalities and authorities and powers, the many-eyed cherubim and
the six-winged seraphim, who with two wings cover their faces, with two cover their feet, and with two fly; they cry out and say one to another: Aloud:
with unceasing lips and never-silent theology, they sing, proclaim, cry out and say the hymn of victory to the glory of your majestic splendour with a radiant voice:
The people shall say: Holy, holy, + holy, + Lord Sabaoth; the heavens are full:
The priest shall recite this prayer: Holy are you, + eternal King and giver of all holiness. Holy is your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.
Holy is your all-holy Spirit, the life-giving Lord, who searches all things, even the depths of your Godhead.
Holy are you, + Almighty and all-powerful, awesome and good; truly + holy are you, who were exceedingly merciful toward your creatures, and who made man from the earth
after your own likeness and image, and granted him the delight and rest of paradise, so that he might have dominion over the creatures you had made and govern the world worthily and
in righteousness. But when he transgressed your commandments and was cast out from there, you did not disregard him or cast him off, O Good One, but you instructed him like a merciful father
and called him through the Law, and became his nurturer through the prophets. And after them, at the last end of the ages, your only-begotten Son himself
you sent into the world, so that he might renew and restore your image. He came down from heaven and became flesh from the Holy Spirit and from Mary, the Mother of God and ever-virgin;
he was born in Bethlehem of Judea, was baptized in the holy Jordan by John, lived among people, and arranged all things for the salvation
of our race. And when he, the sinless one, was about to undergo, in obedience and of his own will, the life-giving death as surety for us sinners:
on the night in which our Lord Jesus Christ was given up for the life of the world, he took bread, lifted it up in his holy and spotless hands
and showed it to you, God and Father; + he gave thanks, + blessed it, + sanctified it, broke it, and gave it to his blessed disciples, the apostles, and said to them:
Aloud: Take and eat, for this is my body, which is broken for you and for many and given for the forgiveness of sins. The people: Amen.
The priest: Likewise, after supper he took the cup mixed with wine and water; + he gave thanks, + blessed it, + sanctified it, gave it to his disciples, the apostles, and said to them:
Aloud: Drink from it, all of you, for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is shed for you and for many and given for the forgiveness of sins.
The people: Amen. The priest shall recite this prayer: Do this in remembrance of me. As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, the death of the Son of Man
you proclaim until he comes. And now we remember his sufferings and his burial, his resurrection on the third day, his ascension into heaven, and [his sitting] at your right hand, O God, and
…[at the right hand of] the Father, and his second coming, glorious and fearful, when he will come to judge the living and the dead, when he will repay each one according to his deeds.
We offer to you, O Lord, this fearful and bloodless sacrifice, so that you may not deal with us according to our sins or repay us according to our iniquities, but according to your
patience and your endless love for humankind, overlook and blot out the sins and errors of those who pray to you, and grant us
those heavenly and eternal gifts which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have entered into the heart of man, which you have prepared, in your mercy, for those who love you.
Exclamation: For your people and your church pray to you. The people: Have mercy on us, O God, Father Almighty.
The priest shall say this prayer: Have mercy on us, O God, according to your great mercy and your abundant compassion, and send down upon us, and upon this fearful
sacrifice and these holy offerings set forth, your Holy Spirit, O Lord, the giver of life, who shares the throne with you, the Father, and with the Son, who reigns with you, co-eternal,
equally without beginning and of one being with you, who spoke in the Law and the Prophets and the New Covenant, who came down upon our Lord Jesus Christ at the Jordan
River in the form of a dove, who came down upon your holy apostles in the likeness of tongues of fire in the upper room of the mystery in the days of Pentecost.
Exclamation: So that now also, by his good and glorious coming, he may bless [+] and sanctify and make this bread the precious body of Christ.
The people: Amen. The priest: And this cup the true blood of Christ. The people: Amen.
The priest shall say this prayer: So that it may be, for all who receive it, for the forgiveness of sins and for eternal life, [+] for the sanctification of souls
and bodies, for bringing forth the fruit of good works, and for the strengthening of your church, which you acquired with the precious blood of your Christ.
Found it upon the rock of faith, so that the gates of hell may not prevail against it, by delivering it from every stumbling block of the heretics who commit lawlessness, until the end of the age.
Here he shall bow: We offer to you, O Lord, this fearful and bloodless sacrifice for your holy places, which you glorified by the manifestation of your Christ, and first of all for holy and glorious
Zion, mother of all the churches, and for your holy, catholic and apostolic church throughout the whole world, and to all the ends of heaven. Grant them abundantly the gift of the Holy Spirit.
O Lord, remember among them our holy fathers, the patriarchate and the orthodox bishops [?], who rightly proclaim, and who truly declared to us the word of truth.

First of all, remember our venerable father the patriarch. Grant him an honourable old age, and keep him with long life for many years, to shepherd your people in all truth, righteousness and holiness.
Remember, O Lord, the holy city of Jerusalem and all cities and villages, and all who live in them in faith, in good conduct and in the fear of Christ, in peace and quiet
Remember here, O Lord, the honourable priests, and also [?] the deacons who serve Christ, and all the orders of the Church who live a humble life, and the Christ-loving people.

Remember me also, O Lord, in your great mercy: me, this sinner and worthless (literally "leftover") servant of yours. Look upon me in your mercy and keep me unharmed by those who pursue me. And whatever sin I have committed against you in word, deed or thought, be merciful to me.
Pardon and forgive me, O Lord, for you are good and love humankind; not with long-suffering [?]. For where sin increased, there your gift abounded all the more.
Remember, O Lord, our pious king and our pious queen and their reign in piety. Take up weapon and shield, and rise up to help
them. Bring all the heathen nations into subjection to them, so that we may live in peace and quiet, in all godliness and dignity.
Remember, O Lord, our fathers and brothers who are struggling in old age and weakness.
Remember also, O Lord, our fathers and brothers who are in prison and in chains, in exile and captivity, and in the caves of the earth.

Remember, O Lord, those who travel by ship and other travellers, those who are in foreign lands and in hardship, and those who have set out on a long journey, our fathers and brothers, who ask you for mercy and help. Remember, O Lord,
those who are tormented by unclean spirits. Set free all the bodies of the sick who are suffering. Have mercy on all who are oppressed. Set all of them free from every kind of
illness, our fathers and brothers, and all Christian souls who are afflicted and grieving and who ask for your mercy and help. Remember them all for good.
Have mercy on all, O Lord. Be gracious to all; look upon all. Give peace to the multitude of your people. Scatter all stumbling blocks; put an end to all wars.
Grant us your peace and love, O God our Saviour.
Remember [them/us] for the good tempering of the air, for peaceful rains, for a good yield of crops, and for a full crown of the year by your sweetness.
For the eyes of all wait upon you, and you give them their food in due season. Remember, O Lord, also those who have brought this offering today
to your holy altar, and those for whom each person has made an offering or whom each has in mind, and those whose names we now read out.
The deacon shall say the commemoration of the living: Remember, O Lord, and have mercy on the donor: these:
of the liturgies: Symeon, Catholicos of Kartli. And have mercy on and magnify John, Bishop of Atskuri, and
Ephrem of Tsilkani. O Lord, have mercy on the servants and ascetics of this desert monastery. O Lord, have mercy on Dachi and Symeon.
The priest shall say this prayer: Remember, O Lord, all these and those we have commemorated, and give them heavenly things instead of earthly ones, instead of corruptible things
incorruptible ones, instead of temporary things eternal ones, according to the gospel of your Christ, for you have power over life and death, O Lord.

Further, make us worthy to commemorate those who have pleased you from the beginning of the world, generation after generation: the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, holy martyrs and confessors; exaltation [?].
Above all, our all-holy, glorious, blessed, incorruptible and most blessed Lady, the Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary. (Said quietly.)
Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you. (Three times.) The holy, blessed John the Forerunner and Baptist.
And the holy apostles Peter, Paul, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James, Simon, Jude and Matthias;
Mark and Luke the evangelist; and the holy prophets and the righteous; holy Stephen, the first deacon and first martyr;
and our holy, blessed fathers, the patriarchs: Moses, Aaron, Joshua, Samuel, David, Elijah, Elisha, Zechariah,
Simeon, and all your saints. The holy martyrs: Saint George, Saint Theodore, Saint Eustathius,
Saint Cyricus, Saint Julitta, Saint Barbara, the holy Forty, Saint Abo, and all your saints,
the confessors of Christ our God, who were martyred for their good confession and confessed well; and the holy women, the myrrh-bearers who brought ointment; Saint Nino. Remember them, O Lord.

Our holy fathers the bishops, from holy James the apostle, son [?] of the Lord and first archbishop, down to the present: the worthy ones who served as bishops in orthodoxy in the holy city of our God.
Remember, O Lord, our holy fathers the teachers: Ignatius, Dionysius, Irenaeus, Gregory, Alexander, Eustathius,
Athanasius, Basil, Gregory, Gregory, Ambrose, Amphilochius, Liberius, Damasus, John, Epiphanius, Theophilus, Celestine,
Augustine, Cyril, Leo, Proclus, Felix, Hormisdas, Ephrem, Sophronius, Agapetus, Eulogius, Martin, Modestus, Peter the martyr,
Nicholas. Remember, O Lord, the six holy and very great councils of the world: the three hundred and eighteen of Nicaea,
the one hundred and fifty of Constantinople, the two hundred of the first council of Ephesus, the six hundred and thirty of Chalcedon, the one hundred and sixty-four of the fifth holy council,
the two hundred and eighty-nine of the sixth holy council; and these holy councils, and our worthy fathers in every place who served as bishops in orthodoxy and who rightly taught the word of truth.
Remember, O Lord, our holy fathers the hermits who lived in the desert: Abba Paul, Antony, Paul, Pachomius, Ammon, Theodore,
Hilarion, Arsenius, Macarius, John, Ephrem, Simeon, Simeon, Theodosius, Chariton, Euthymius, Theoctistus, Sabbas, Dometius, Gerasimus, Gelasius,
and those who were killed by barbarians on the holy mountain of Sinai. It is not that we are in any way worthy to commemorate their blessedness, but
so that they, standing boldly before your dreadful and awesome throne, may remember us too, wretched as we are.
Remember the presbyters, deacons, subdeacons, deaconesses, readers, monks, interpreters, exorcists, God-loving
virgins, and those lawfully married, who have died in the communion of the holy catholic and apostolic Church.
Remember, O Lord, the pious and faithful emperors: Constantine, Helena, Theodosius the Great, Marcian, Pulcheria, Leo, Justinian,
and the pious and faithful emperors who reigned after them; and all who have fallen asleep before us in Christ,
the lay people; and those for whom each person has made an offering or has in mind; and those whose names we are now reading out.
The deacon shall read out the names of the departed, and the priest shall commemorate the name of whomever he wishes.
O Lord, remember the souls of Zachariah and Mary and of all their departed children.
Give rest to the souls of Theodore and Febronia and of all their departed children, and to the soul of Catholicos Symeon and of all his sisters and brothers.

O Lord God of our fathers and of all flesh, remember all these: those whom we have remembered and those whom we have not. Give them rest there, and make them worthy of the land of the living, the kingdom of heaven, the bosom of Abraham,
Isaac and Jacob, from which all pains, sorrows and afflictions have fled away, where the light of your face looks on them.
O Lord, make our end Christian, without sin and without affliction. Guide us, O Lord, and gather us under the wings
of your elect, when you wish and as you wish, only without shame and without sins, before the throne of your Christ.
Exclamation: Through the grace, mercy and love for humankind of your Christ, with whom glory befits you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen. Priest: Peace to all. People: And with your spirit. Deacon, this: Again and always, let us all together pray to the Lord.
People: Kyrie eleison. For this holy, offered, sanctified, glorious, heavenly gift, let us all together pray to the Lord. People: Kyrie eleison.

That the Lord our God, who has received these on his holy, invisible, heavenly and spiritual altar as a sweet spiritual fragrance, may send down on us the grace and gift of the Holy Spirit, let us all together [pray] to the Lord.

People: Kyrie eleison. Let us ask the Lord for the unity of the faith and the communion of the all-holy Spirit, and let us commit ourselves and our whole life to Christ our God. People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: O God and Father of our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, who sit upon the cherubim and are glorified by the seraphim, before whom
stand thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads of holy angels and the hosts of archangels: these offerings, gifts and fruits that have been offered to you,
receive them as a sweet fragrance and sanctify them by the grace of your Christ and by the coming of the Holy Spirit. Sanctify, O Lord, our souls and bodies, and examine our minds,
test our thoughts, and remove from me [?] every wicked mind of ours, every defiled thought, every impure desire, all envy, pride,
duplicity, every lie, every deceit, every burden of this world, all greed, every stirring of the flesh and of the spirit, and everything foreign to your holy will.

Exclamation: And make us worthy, O Lord, with boldness, with a pure heart, with an unenlightened [?] soul, with an unashamed face and sanctified lips, to dare to call on you, the heavenly God, the holy and merciful Father, and to say: People: Our Father…
The priest shall say this prayer: And lead us not into temptation, O Lord, Lord of hosts, but deliver us from the evil one and from his works, for your name has been called upon us in our lowliness.
Exclamation: For yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
People: Amen. Priest: Peace to all. People: And with your spirit. Deacon: Let us bow our heads to the Lord. People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: Your servants and handmaids bow the necks of their hearts to you, and they await from you the great mercy of your riches. Your spiritual blessing
send, O Lord, and sanctify our souls and [?] and bodies, so that we may be made worthy of communion in your incorruptible mysteries, for the forgiveness of our sins and as the way to eternal life.
Exclamation: For you are worthy of worship and glorified, our God, your only-begotten Son and your all-holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. People: Amen.
Priest: The grace of the + holy, consubstantial and worshipful + Trinity be with you all. People: And with your spirit. Deacon: Let us attend.
The priest shall say this prayer: O Holy One, who rest among the holy, O Lord, sanctify our souls by the word of your grace, so that your all-holy Spirit may be planted [in us].
You said, "Be holy," for you are holy, O ineffable God, Word of the Father, consubstantial, coexistent and co-ruling with the Holy Spirit. Accept from me
the hymn of the holy and bloodless sacrifice, the unceasing hymn, together with the cherubim and seraphim, of me, a sinful and unworthy servant, the word that cries aloud.
Exclamation: The holy things for the holy. People: One is holy, one is the Lord, Jesus Christ, to the glory of God the Father, with the Holy Spirit, to whom be glory to the ages of ages. Amen.
The priest shall lift up the prosphora and say the Creed. People: Kyrie eleison, 12 times. He shall break the holy bread and put it into the chalice.
He shall make the sign of the cross with it over the Blood and say: The Body and Blood of Christ are united, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
Blessed is the Father. Blessed is the Son. Blessed is the Holy Spirit. Let every breath and every creature praise the Lord. Alleluia.
Prayer of the Fraction, spoken by Saint Athanasius, archbishop.
O Lord God, lover of mankind, and Redeemer, Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who appeared as Savior for us and enlightened the whole
world: you did very great wonders and mercies toward us, so that you might completely set us free from slavery to death.
You, the holy and spotless Lamb of God, appeared for our sake in human nature; like a sheep you were led to the slaughter in your precious Body and Blood.
You, the Righteous One, were crucified like an evildoer among thieves.
Yes, O Lord, before your crucifixion you took bread in your holy, spotless hands, blessed it, gave it to your blessed disciples and said: "This is my Body."
And after eating the bread, you took the cup, mixed with wine and water, in your holy and spotless hands, blessed it, gave it to those same blessed disciples of yours and said: "This
is my Blood. Do this in remembrance of me. As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, proclaim the death of the Son of Man until he comes."
And now we remember that blessing and your commandments. But I, if only I had that shame in spirit for my most evil sins and abominations
I am not worthy to look up. But to you alone I say in confession: I have sinned, O Lord, O Lord, and I know my iniquities, and that unworthily and rashly
I presume to approach this ineffable mystery, your precious body and true blood. Yet by faith I have hope in that incomprehensible
mercy and love for mankind of yours, and we ask of you, O Lord, Lord Jesus Christ: have mercy on me, O Lord, have mercy, and do not condemn me for my unworthy rashness.
But may this holy, true, precious body and blood of yours be for me a stripping-away of sins, an erasing of my iniquities, an enlightening of the eyes of my mind, so that I may be cleansed of sin
great and impure, and may I always fear you, flee from all sin, and long all the more for this precious body and blood of yours, and always speak in my heart of the kingdom of heaven.
For yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, here and always and to the ages of ages.
The deacon shall say: "In the peace of Christ let us sing." They shall say "Taste and see." Prayer when the priest himself takes communion: Holy, holy, holy,
ineffable Trinity, grant me to receive this body and blood for salvation and not for condemnation. Grant me to do what is pleasing, so that I may
appear pleasing to you and live by doing your commandments, and boldly call upon you as God and Father, and call upon your name and your will.

Hallowed be your name upon me, O Lord, for you are mighty and praised and glorified. Holy is your name, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
At the communion of the bishop: The true body and blood of the Son of God and our Savior Jesus Christ is given to the high priest
of Christ our God, for the guarding of your office in holiness and righteousness, for the remission of sins and for eternal life.
For a priest: The body and blood of God and our Savior Jesus Christ, the Son of God, is given to the priest of Christ our God for the remission of sins and for eternal life. For a deacon:

The precious body and blood of Christ our God, who said, "Where I am, there also will my servant be," is given to you for the guarding of your diaconate in holiness, for the remission of sins and for eternal life.
And when he brings down the chalice for communion, he shall make the sign of the cross, give the peace, and say: "I will exalt you, my God, my King."
And when they take communion, the deacon shall say: "Let us draw near in the fear of Christ." The people: "Before you, O Lord."
And when they have taken communion, the deacon shall say: "Kyrie eleison." The priest says this: "You are exalted in the heavens, O God, and over all the earth."
The priest shall make the sign of the cross and say: "Let our mouth be filled with praise, so that we may sing." After communion the deacon shall lead the litany and say this:

Stand upright, we who have received this holy and glorious, heavenly, incorruptible, life-giving mystery of the Lord our God Jesus Christ. Let us give thanks to the Lord God of all. The people: We thank you, O Lord.

That this holy [gift] which we are to receive may be for our salvation, for the crushing of our enemy, for the forgiveness of our sins, and for receiving the Holy Spirit, let us all pray together to the Lord.
People: Kyrie eleison. [Commemorating] our all-holy, glorious, blessed, incorruptible, most blessed Lady, the Mother of God. People: To you, O Lord.
The priest shall say this prayer: O God, who in your great mercy forgive the weakness of your servants and have made us worthy to receive this heavenly
[gift] from the altar, do not condemn us sinners for receiving your incorruptible mysteries. Instead, keep us, O good Lord, in your holiness and
righteousness, so that we may become worthy of your Holy Spirit and share in it, and may find a portion, an inheritance and grace with all your saints in the light of your face,
through the mercy and love for humankind of your Christ, with whom glory is fitting to you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Ekphonesis (said aloud):
For you are blessed and holy, and glorified is your all-honourable and most magnificent name, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever.
People: Amen. Priest: Peace be with all. People: And with your spirit.
Deacon: Let us bow our heads to the Lord. People: To you, O Lord. The priest shall say this prayer:
O God, who are great and wonderful, look upon your servants, for we have bowed our heads to you. Stretch out your mighty hand and your exalted arm for the salvation of the human race,
the hand that is full of blessing. Bless your people and guard your inheritance, so that at all times we may bless you, the only living and true God, the holy Trinity, one in essence.
Ekphonesis (said aloud): For to you belongs every offering of glory, honour and worship, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever.
People: Amen. Deacon: Let us keep ourselves in the peace of Christ. People: In the name of the Lord, O Lord, bless us.
Then they shall dismiss the people. After the dismissal they shall go into the diaconicon. The deacon shall lead the litany, and the priest shall say this prayer:
For you have given us, O Lord, holiness and a share in the holy body and precious blood of your Christ. Give us also the grace of your Holy
Spirit. Keep us blameless in the faith, lead us to the attainment of all perfection, and to rest in the age to come,

by the grace, mercy and love for humankind of your Christ, with whom glory is fitting to you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen. Prayer at the gathering up of the holy [gifts]:
I thank you, O Lord, giver of the gifts of eternal light, who labour for souls, guide of the saints. Give us eyes of understanding so that we may see you, and ears that listen to you alone,
so that our soul may be filled with your grace. Establish a pure heart within us, O God, so that we may be established in your riches, O wonderful God who loves humankind.

Adorn our souls and calm our minds, keeping us unwavering, your servants who give thanks to you. For blessed is your kingdom, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.
Litany: at the blessing (ordination) of a bishop, a priest, or a deacon: Let us pray to the Lord: [?] us from heaven.
For the life of our worthy father in Christ, Simeon, Catholicos of Kartli, and for God's mercy upon him from above, and for the success of the works of his hands, let us pray to the Lord.
And for the one on whom hands are now being laid, that his faith may be firm, let us pray to the Lord.
That the Lord may grant him a holy, spotless, and undefiled ministry, let us pray to the Lord.
For the offering of our prayers and for the forgiveness of sins, let us pray to the Lord.
Our all-holy, glorious, blessed, incorruptible, and most blessed Lady, the Theotokos [Mother of God]. The bishop shall give thanks, and the deacon
shall say aloud: By the mercy of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; by the intercession of the holy Theotokos, the ever-virgin Mary;
by the powers of the life-giving and venerable Cross of Mtskheta; by the grace and faith of the holy catholic church;
by the intercession of holy John the Baptist and of holy Stephen, the first deacon and first martyr;
by the intercession of all the holy prophets, apostles, bearers [?], patriarchs, and martyrs;
by the command, the choice, and the laying on of hands of our worthy father in Christ, Simeon, Catholicos of Kartli, and with the testimony and support

(if a bishop is present, he shall name him; if not, then) of these priests: this our brother (he shall say his name, and the church to which he belongs) is blessed from the lay state to the office of reader;
from the office of reader to subdeacon; from the office of subdeacon to archdeacon; from the office of archdeacon to priest; from the priesthood to chorepiscopus [assistant bishop];
from the office of chorepiscopus to bishop, in the house of the holy catholic church, as a servant of the holy churches and as one who prays for all Christians.
Let us all pray for him, that the Lord may have mercy. He shall say this three times: Lord, have mercy. And: Worthy. And when hands are laid on someone as bishop,
priest, or deacon, the bishop shall first say this prayer: The grace of God, which heals the weak and makes up what is lacking,
lays hands on this our son (he shall say his name, and the church to which he belongs). And he shall pronounce the judgment upon those who chose him and testified for him. The blessing of a reader.
The first order of the holy church is the office of reader. For this reason you must hold the divine books in your hands with reverence and walk in the first
path, so that those who listen to you may find edification, and so that you may gain for yourself a greater rank. Never bring shame on this ordination
of yours. Live your life with care, holiness, and righteousness, so that God, who loves mankind, may be merciful to you and you may attain a higher ministry.
Second prayer: O Lord Almighty, sanctify this your servant (name), and choose him, you who are holy and glorious. Make him worthy of all wisdom and knowledge, so that he may read your divine

words and keep them entirely without blemish, by the mercy and love for mankind of your Christ, with whom glory is fitting to you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
At the appointment of a subdeacon: the bishop shall say on Sunday, so that all the people hear:
You, son, who are now like the deacons: keep yourself in the fear of God. Do the works of the Gospel in holiness. Keep yourself pure. Keep holiness with understanding, and learn humility.
Keep to worship, and do not neglect fasting, so that the Lord may give you rest and raise you to the greater honour. And the people say: So be it, so be it.
Blessing for the appointment of a subdeacon. O God of powers, God of truth, God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and of all his righteous offspring,
God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Father of mercies and God of all comfort: look upon this your servant, by name [N.], who is being sealed
as subdeacon. Grant him the seal of the subdeacon, so that he may serve with confidence at the door of your holy church, and so that, having been proven, he may advance to the greater rank.
For to you belong all glory, honour and worship, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever.
Second blessing for the office of subdeacon. Look upon this servant and choose him, O Lord Almighty, and make him distinguished in good works, so that he may fulfil this ministry
by your will and your working, through the mercy and favour of your Christ. With him, glory is fitting to you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever.
Blessing for the appointment of a deaconess.
O Lord God of powers, you commanded Mary, the sister of Moses, to be the first of all women to cry out in praise of you. You gave the grace of prophecy to Deborah.
In this new covenant also, you laid down as a law through your Holy Spirit that deacons should be appointed who are not double-tongued and not slaves to much wine, but teachers
of good things, so that they may be an example of every virtue. You yourself appoint this your handmaid to anoint with oil those who come to your holy baptism, and
to lead them to your holy font, and to be a deacon in your church, following the rule of Phoebe, whom the apostle appointed as servant of Cenchreae.
Grant her also to reprove with care, and to instruct the young in the labour of your works. Grant her that everything she says may be done in your name,

so that, having served well and without fault, she may find confidence of help in that hour at the right hand of your Christ. With him you are blessed, together with the all-holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever.
Second blessing for the office of deaconess. You created all things by the word of your command, and through the incarnation and the struggle of your only-begotten Son
you made man and woman holy and equal, as it pleased you. You gave the grace of your Holy Spirit not only to men but also to women.
Now also appoint this your handmaid to this ministry, O Lord Almighty, and give her the grace of the Spirit, so that she may walk in [?] of righteousness,
through the mercy and favour of your Christ. With him, glory is fitting to you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever.

Third blessing for the office of deaconess. O Lord Almighty, you adorned your church also with the ministry of the diaconate, and you filled the multitude of churches with the grace of your Holy Spirit:

You yourself, O Lord, appoint this your handmaid N. to the ministry of the diaconate. Grant her, with reverence and holiness, that beautiful ministry; receive her to fulfil it; guide her zeal well; give her the strength to endure.
For to you belongs all glory, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
On the archdeacon: whoever is appointed must be vouched for by the priests of the church for which he is designated to serve at the holy altar. He must be the husband of one wife,

holy, blameless and not disobedient. He must have proven himself in the work of caring for the sick, and must labour on behalf of orphans and widows. He must keep watch through night vigils, be steadfast in prayer and fasting, and be patient

in the teaching of his teachers, a reverent disciple, and one who administers by carrying out the order of the church. When he has fulfilled all this, then he may become worthy to be appointed to the rank of archdeacon.
Blessing of the archdeacon, 1. Through you, O Lord, many forms of grace are granted for every need of your church. You revealed the diaconate's
ministry in the likeness of limbs to limbs: of teachers, deacons, priests and ministers. Give the grace of the diaconate to your servant N. Make him worthy to serve
at your altar, to carry out what you have commanded with true love and zeal and without shame, and to advance to the higher rank, ever strengthened
in that perfection which comes from Christ. For blessed, holy and glorious is your name, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
Blessing of the archdeacon, 2. O God, who created all things and adorned them by the word, who rest in the incorruptible ages, who
gave us the ministry of eternal life through your prophets, who enlightened us with the light of knowledge, O God, creator of glorious things and of all,
Creator, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who sent him to serve your will so that he might save the whole race of humankind, and who revealed
to us your counsel, your power, your wisdom and your providence: your beloved Son Jesus Christ, the only-begotten, Lord of light, ruler of rulers, Lord of lordships and
God of gods. O Lord, give the spirit of grace and zeal to this your servant, so that zeal, goodness, courage and strength may be given to him to please you.

O Lord, give him works of righteousness according to the law, gentleness without shame, love for orphans, love of good ministry, mercy toward widows, and a love of the good with a fervent heart. And enlighten

this man whom you were pleased to choose to serve the church, to offer in holiness your holy things [?] from the portion offered to you, of your receiving [?], so that blamelessly, in holiness and worthily, with a pure mind,
he may serve and receive greater honour through your Son Jesus Christ our Lord, through whom glory is due to you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
Blessing of the archdeacon, the third. O Lord God Almighty, who have kept your mercy for those who fear your name, who granted
to humankind the knowledge of your truth through the coming and incarnation of your only-begotten Son, and who appointed apostles to establish the holy
[?] your [?], and they appointed deacons as ministers of your holiness by counsel: first Stephen and those with him. They blessed them and appointed them to this ministry. And now also
choose and appoint your servant by the grace of the Holy Spirit to the ministry of your holiness, so that he may minister at your altar with holy intent,
so that he may be distinguished in good works, to the glory of your holy name, and so that he may find your good things from above on that day of recompense, through the mercy and
acceptance of your Christ, with whom glory befits you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen. As a priest or as a bishop: whoever

is appointed must be attested by all the people. As was said before, he must be the husband of one wife: holy, blameless, and not neglectful [?] of the care of the sick, tested, and one who works hard for orphans and widows.
And if he has been like a father to the church, a quiet and holy minister, then this one is worthy. Let it be said three times.
At the revelation of the virtue that befits him: so that they may be made worthy of the grace [?] of rejoicing;
so that they may be vessels of the all-holy Spirit, and may have and bear the cross of the only-begotten Son of God, Jesus Christ. The ordination of a priest shall be done in this way:
They shall bring them before the holy altar. The bishop shall lay hands on their heads, and they shall bow their necks and be blessed with this blessing:
Blessing for the presbyterate, 1: You, O Lord, whom the heavenly ones serve by thousands and by myriads,
you also ordained the earthly ministry and appointed priests for the people as overseers of true worship. We ask you now also, O Lord: give to your servant
[?] your Holy Spirit, so that he may carry out the ministry as the apostles did, with true teaching, and gather together your [?] with his own zeal, by the power
of your grace and the love for humankind of your Christ, to whom glory befits, together with your all-holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
Blessing for the presbyterate, 2: O God, and Power of our Lord Jesus Christ, ineffable light, who have neither beginning nor end, O Lord, who set a law
as a boundary for everything and by your will laid down an order for all that you created: hear us and look upon this your servant. Give him the spirit of grace and
of counsel and of courage, the spirit of the presbyterate, unaging, unfailing, self-existent [?], loving faith, teaching and revelation, to help and labour [?] for your people
with singleness of heart and with fear, with a pure heart, with holiness, dignity and wisdom, through the oversight of your Holy Spirit and of your foreknowledge, O Lord, just as
you looked upon the chosen people, O Lord, and commanded Moses to choose elders, and you filled them with your Holy Spirit and granted it to your servant. And now, O Lord, give the unfailing
Spirit of yours that you gave to your disciples, and through them to all who truly believe in you. Make this man worthy to be filled with your wisdom and your mystery, to shepherd
your people worthily and in truth, and to praise, sing hymns to, give thanks to and glorify your name day and night, so that he may labour [?] with joy and patience, and so that he may be a vessel
of the Holy Spirit and may have and bear the cross of your only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ, through whom glory and power befit you to all the ages. Amen.
Blessing for the priesthood. 3. O Lord Almighty, holy and glorious, who created heaven and earth, the sea and everything that is in them, who
established your holy church and revealed in it apostles, prophets and priests, for the establishing and perfecting of the saints:
You, God of hosts and King of glory, visit now also and look upon your servant, and choose him by the choosing of the descent, so that your Holy Spirit may dwell in him. Give
him the word of teaching when he opens his mouth, and make him perfect as a chosen priest, O Lord Almighty, so that he may lay his hand on the sick and they may be healed, and so that he may serve
your holy altar and, with a worthy heart and mind, offer to you this bloodless and rational sacrifice, and be enlightened in works of righteousness for the building up

of your holy church and for the glorifying of your awesome name, O Lord, so that he may be able [to stand] on that day of manifestation, by reason of this [?], at which you have made him worthy to stand, your holy
altar, through the grace and mercy of your only-begotten Son, with whom glory befits you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
Blessing for a chorepiscopus. O Lord God Almighty, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, before whom stand myriads upon myriads of angels and archangels, who dwell in light that cannot be spoken of:
make this servant of yours also worthy of the greater honour of the priesthood, O God Almighty, so that your Holy Spirit may come upon him, and so that with a pure heart he may serve your holy
altar and in holiness offer your holy mystery. Bless this servant of yours, O Lord; grant him the grace of the chorepiscopate, worthy, holy and pleasing:
Give him a watchful mind and your service, so that he may be able to teach others too. Give him, O Lord, worthiness, holiness, goodness, gentleness, long-suffering, patience,

hope, and love for you, God, and for his neighbour as for himself, so that he may be a father to orphans and a caretaker [?] of your [people?], steadfast [?] in night vigils, diligent in prayer, careful:
and that he may offer worship, glory, thanks and honour to you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Blessing for the chorepiscopate. 2. O God, great benefactor and creator of all honour, Maker, God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who are ineffable
light, who prepare in advance every honour and crown for those who ask them of you in faith: in fear we beseech you and pray to you, hear the prayer
of ours and look upon your servant N., who is attested and made worthy of the chorepiscopate. O Lord, give the spirit of grace, of power and of knowledge, the spirit
of godliness, the spirit of wisdom and of zeal to this servant of yours, so that he may be given diligence, holiness, zeal, virtue, courage and power, through Christ Jesus
our Lord, almighty and enlightener of our souls, through whom glory and power befit you, together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
Blessing for the episcopate and for the catholicosate.

O God, who created all things by your power and established the world by your counsel; who adorned the crown of the things you created; who gave them the fear of obedience to you and the keeping of it:
who granted us true understanding and made known to us your sweet Holy Spirit; who sent down your beloved Son as Savior [?], the only-begotten, the undefiled, for our salvation:
O God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, God of mercies and of all comfort, who dwell on high in those incorruptible holy treasuries, who are exalted and glorious,
fearful and great, and overseeing all; who knew all things before they came to be, from whom all things came into being; who gave enlightenment in the church of grace through your only-begotten Son:
You appointed from the beginning those who had chosen righteousness beforehand, and those who are doers of holiness, to dwell in your dwellings. You chose Abraham, who
was pleasing to you by faith, and you brought the virgin Enoch to the treasury of life. You appointed rulers and priests in holiness in your heights, O Lord. You called
the rulers to the place of your glory to sing and glorify your name and the name of your only-begotten Son. O Lord, from that time on you did not leave your holiness on high without ministry
before the creation of the world, O God; and again, from the creation of the world, you adorned your holiness with rulers and faithful priests, as an image of your heavenly holy things.

You, O Lord, have now willed to be glorified, and have made this man worthy to be ruler of your people. Enlighten him, and give him, from your princely Spirit, understanding and the grace that you gave to your beloved Son Jesus Christ.

Give him wisdom, O God, counsel, courage, power of spirit, unity, so that all things may be under your watchful care. Give him, O Holy One, of your Spirit, which you bestowed on your holy apostles, for the undefiled
and holy church of yours and for every place of your holiness. Grant to this your servant, O Lord, that he may be pleasing to you, glorifying and praising you without ceasing, O God, with hymns
that are fitting, with accepted prayers, faithful petitions, right counsel, and a humble heart, in the work of life, peace and truth, knowing sincerity.

O Father, who know the hearts, [look] upon this your servant, whom you have chosen as bishop, so that he may shepherd your holy flock and serve you as high priest, blamelessly and in holiness, without ceasing,
ministering day and night, and making your face manifest. Make him worthy, O Lord, to offer the holy offering to your church reverently and with all fear, so that he may have the spirit of authority.
Grant him the power to loose every bond, as you granted it to your holy apostles, so that he may be pleasing to you. Strengthen him with gentleness, love, learning, knowledge and courage,

to embrace [?] the people, so that he may mourn for the ignorant and call upon you as helper [?], and offer prayer to you as a sweet-smelling savor, through your beloved Son Jesus Christ, through whom
glory and power befit you, together with your Holy Spirit, both before the ages and now and always, and from generation to generation, to the endless ages of ages. Amen.
Blessing of a bishop, the second. O God, who are great and eternal, from whom nothing is hidden, who created all things by the word of your command,
who do far more than we ask or understand, who established the churches by the precious blood of your Only-begotten, and
raised up teachers in them, through whom the knowledge of your truth spread to all the ends of heaven. This knowledge your only-begotten
Son himself graciously gave to the human race. From among each and every generation of people he revealed your chosen ones.

You yourself, O God, look now also on this your servant, and choose him by that choosing of the Holy Spirit, so that he may be a high priest like that true shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep.
Confirm him in this holy and glorious ministry by that Spirit of your only-begotten Son, so that he may shepherd your flock with an upright mind.
Guide him in the words of truth, and give him speech worthy of the opening [of his mouth] [?], so that he may give light to those who sit in darkness and be a teacher of the foolish
and an instructor of infants. Arm him and clothe him with power from heaven, so that whenever he lays his hand on the sick, signs and wonders may take place among your people, so that he may teach
fully and confirm spiritually everything. By your will you have chosen him from our poverty to be a faithful [steward] of your riches and a shepherd of your people,
so that he may stand before your holy altar on that dreadful day of your revelation and wait for the good reward, together with those who have laboured faithfully, through your
love for humankind and the mercy and acceptance of your only-begotten Son. With him glory is fitting for you, with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
Blessing of a bishop, the third. This prayer is said if a bishop is being consecrated:
the archbishop shall say it. If a catholicos is being consecrated, the bishop of Manglisi shall say it.

You who granted Israel the gift of high priesthood of the bodily ministry [and] have appointed us [?], hear us, O Lord. Establish your servant [Name] as a shepherd, a faithful minister and a guardian of the faith,
a champion of your Church, a gatherer of strangers, and a protector of your saints and faithful people, so that he may receive the grace of your Christ and make your Church grow

with the help of the Spirit of holiness, and may be presented to the glory of your Christ. To him belongs the glory of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages.
After the laying on of hands for a bishop, a priest or a deacon, when he has said the three prayers and conferred this rank, he shall say this prayer:
O Lord God of hosts, who adorned with beauty your holy Church, and through it those who serve in it, number also this one who has now had hands laid on him, by the Spirit
of the all-good order of peace. For you are the one who gives light, and glory is fitting for you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Blessing of the hodikon [?], that is, the portable altar carried on journeys.
The new altar is to be placed on top of the holy old altar. At the dedication of the church, these are the psalms to be recited. As the first psalm they shall say:
"How lovely are [thy dwellings]" ... ending: "Blessed is the man who hopes in thee."
Four priests shall lift up the altar, with the censer and candles carried before it. They shall go around the altar once, set it on the holy altar, and say a litany and a prayer.
Then they shall take up the second psalm: "Lord, remember David and all [his meekness]" ... ending: "but upon him shall my holiness flourish."
They shall lift up the altar, go around a second time, and set it on the altar again. They shall say a litany and a prayer, and then take up the third psalm:
"Judge me, O Lord, for I am blameless" ... ending: "In the church I will bless thee, O Lord."
They shall lift up the altar, go around a third time, and set it on the altar. They shall say a litany and a prayer, and the bishop shall bless it with this blessing:
O Lord God of hosts, Creator of all created things, who alone didst stretch out the heavens and didst found the earth upon its own firmness:

thou, O Lord, didst establish cities and villages and raise up churches. Thou didst set up altars in them and command that sacrifices and bloodless offerings be offered for the sake of thy holy name, for the redemption of the human race.
Now, O Lord of all, look upon this odik [altar-table?] and sanctify it by thy Holy Spirit, so that in mountains and caves and clefts, at sea and in all places of thy dominion
the bloodless sacrifice of thy only-begotten Son may be performed upon it, for communion and for the forgiveness of sins of all, together with the holiness
of knowledge of those who offer before thee together, for the sake of unity and communion: the divine mystery that is performed upon it. For thou alone art God,
long-suffering, abounding in mercy and true, the giver of all holiness. To thee we offer up glory and thanksgiving, together with that same only-begotten Son of thine and
thy all-holy, good, life-giving and consubstantial Spirit, now and always and unto ages of ages. Then he shall pour the chrism in three places in the shape of a cross.

The priests shall anoint it and say the same words as in the other blessing of an altar. When they have vested it and set it on that same holy altar, the deacon shall say: "Let us bow our heads to the Lord."
The bishop shall recite this prayer: O Master of glory and Lord of mercies, our God, Almighty, who wast pleased to sanctify this table by the power
of the coming of thy all-holy [Spirit?] [?]: grant to all who partake from it hereafter right faith, a pure heart, and purity of conscience, of body
and of soul, forgiveness of all sins, and joy and gladness of life, through thy only-begotten Son, our Lord and God and Saviour Jesus
Christ, with whom glory and might befit thee forever, together with thy all-holy and consubstantial Spirit, now and always and unto ages of ages. Amen.
O holy high priest, first consecrator, and those whom God wills to be clothed in this vestment and to celebrate the liturgy with this same liturgy:
For the love of God, remember my wretched soul in your holy mysteries, by the name of Simeon the Catholicos, so that grace and blessing from God may be granted to you as well. Amen.
I, Simeon, by Christ Catholicos of Kartli, wrote these holy liturgies for celebration by a hierarch, and [gave] a complete vestment, as is fitting, with a phelonion,

with an orarion, a gingili [?], an enkeri [?], an omophorion, a veil, cuffs [?], a cloth to spread, and a hand towel, as is fitting for a hierarch. I offered and deposited all of it, with nothing lacking.
